p.title: How an earthquake happens

nodes.text: Rocks pull opposite ways at a fault
nodes.info: Rocks on two sides of a fault try to move in opposite directions. A fault is a sharp break in crustal rocks.
Friction locks them; stress builds up. The blocks cannot move yet.
Stress overcomes friction: blocks shift suddenly at the focus. The focus (hypocentre) is where energy is released, inside the earth.
Waves travel out in all directions. Body waves, then surface waves.
The epicentre, right above the focus, feels them first. The point on the surface nearest the focus.
Waves reaching the surface are recorded.
